title: Rethinking The SaaS Apocalypse
summary: While AI-assisted development tools have made it faster to build software prototypes, the article argues that this speed masks the hidden complexity of long-term maintenance, integration, and compliance that remains expensive and difficult. Enterprise software companies will not disappear because core operational systems require stability and ongoing support that internally-built alternatives cannot reliably provide. The real value of SaaS lies in managing the operational environment—regulatory changes, API updates, cybersecurity threats—not in the initial build.
central_argument: AI accelerates only the visible layer of software development; enterprise software companies survive because they manage the invisible complexity of maintenance, integration, compliance, and regulatory adaptation that internally-built systems cannot.
key_claims: AI has made code-writing and initial UI development fast, but does not solve architecture, reliability, integration, compliance, or long-term maintainability
The majority of software development cost and effort occurs after version one, not during initial build
Maintenance of software spanning multiple applications increases in complexity and cost, especially when APIs and business rules change
Companies are not replacing core operational systems (ERP, warehouse management, order management) with AI-built alternatives but rather extending existing platforms
The companies storing decades of mission-critical business data are not going away because moving that data is expensive, slow, and risky
key_tensions: The dangerous illusion that building software quickly means building software that works
The false equivalence between internal builds and enterprise software solutions when accounting for total cost of ownership and risk
